summary: A schedule keeps its reached occurrences when its parent run is automatically superseded: the replacement run's same-named schedule continues every predecessor's history, so publishing a new parent revision no longer replays an already reached tick.

replay.detail: No claim kinds or fields change. Schedules read existing schedule.occurrence-reached claims of the same-named schedule in every run their owner supersedes, following existing mission-run.supersede-linked lineage.

schema.detail: No schema, index or projection change.

rules.detail: Schedule arming, the due-time recheck and the replication-block warning compute the last reached occurrence across the owner's supersession ancestry instead of only the owner's own schedule subject. Explicit work revise and same-run revisions keep their existing schedule subject and history.

compatibility.detail: No API or response change. An older owner still replays the reached tick after automatic supersession; upgraded owners do not.

downtime.detail: No migration or restart requirement beyond the ordinary upgrade.

recovery.detail: No new state or recovery path.
